stops.note: 'heat', the root also of 'caloric', the invisible heat-fluid that 18th-century chemists believed in
the physicist Nicolas Clément defined it in his Paris lectures on heat engines, published in 1824
entered English in 1863 through a translation of Ganot's French physics textbook; the American chemist Wilbur Atwater later measured the energy in foods in calories

current_meaning: a unit of energy, especially of the energy value of food
